questions.question: Describe how the first farmers built their houses.
questions.expected_answer: They pushed a ring of wooden poles into the ground and wove thin sticks between them to make the wattle, then plastered it with mud, clay and cattle dung, the daub. The roof was a cone of poles covered with grass thatch. Floors were earth mixed with cattle dung, beaten and polished smooth. Some houses were beehive-shaped domes of saplings covered in thatch.

questions.question: Describe the layout of a homestead.
questions.expected_answer: A homestead was the home of one large family. Its houses were arranged in a circle or horseshoe around the cattle kraal in the centre. Grain was stored in pits in the kraal or in raised granaries. The main house was at the top of the slope, opposite the kraal entrance, and the homestead entrance was lower down. Fields and grazing were outside.

questions.question: Explain how homesteads, villages and chiefdoms fitted together.
questions.expected_answer: A homestead was one family's home. Several homesteads near each other, often of related families, formed a village, led by a headman. Villages followed a chief, and the chief, his people and their land formed a chiefdom.
